description:
The HUD speed readout on the /fly page shows 'NaN km/s' for outer-planet destinations (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, and asteroids/ dwarf planets beyond ~2.5 AU) for the entire mission duration.

Expected: The speed readout displays a valid finite number (km/s) for every mission destination, including outer planets, at every point along the trajectory.

Acceptance criteria:
- The heliocentric speed computation returns a non-NaN, finite value for every heliocentric distance r encountered on any outer-planet mission trajectory (r up to at least 40 AU), given the existing hardcoded Earth-Mars transfer semi-major axis a ≈ 1.262 AU. [code-invariant: Math.sqrt of a negative radicand returns NaN (IEEE 754), which propagates through toFixed(2) as the string 'NaN' in the HUD — the app must not display NaN in a numeric readout.]
- The specific NaN-producing scenario is when the spacecraft's heliocentric distance r exceeds twice the transfer-ellipse semi-major axis a (2a ≈ 2.524 AU), which occurs on every outer-planet trajectory because the hardcoded a is only valid for Earth→Mars. [reporter: "Flying out to the outer planets, the HUD speed readout just says 'NaN km/s' the whole way" and "the speed function's out-of-range behavior (NaN when radius exceeds apohelion)"]
